figures.caption: Table 4 COMPARISONS WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART COLONOSCOPY ANATOMICAL SEGMENT DETECTION MODELS, WITH MEAN VALUES FROM 5-FOLD CROSS-VALIDATION EXPERIMENTS. OUR METHOD, IN BOLD, SHOWS STATE-OF-THE-ART RESULTS IN COMPARISON TO PREVIOUSLY-USED METHODS. SECOND-BEST RESULTS ARE SHOWN WITH UNDERLINE.

Fig. 1 Illustration of flexures and colo-segments of the lower digestive tract. Colonoscopy procedures begin with the entrance of the colonoscope through the anus, and progresses to the ileocecal region before withdrawal. Sample images from each flexure and colo-segment show great resemblance between the entire length of the colon, with haustral fold differences slightly aiding in differentiation.

Fig. 4 Illustration of attention mechanisms. Local and global attention mechanisms have previously been used by LTContext for action segmentation, but still leave gaps during full sequence analysis. Our Full-Temp module uses local, global, and random attention to better approximate full self-attention on the long colonoscopy video for more comprehensive sequence analysis.

Fig. 3 Our ST-ColoNet framework. Frames are extracted from colonoscopy videos and subsequently acts as input to a two-branched spatial feature extractor employing triplet loss, which is able to extract edge-mediated features. The resultant edge-mediated spatial features undergo processing by a temporal feature extractor enhanced with windowed attention, global attention, and random attention mechanisms.
